item.text: {"search_note":"No separate gap/search explanation was supplied in the M3 research note.","evidence":[{"title":"World Bank Helps Bangladesh Provide Basic Services, Opportunities, and Build Resilience for Displaced Rohingya and Host Communities","publisher":"World Bank","date":"May 28, 2024","url":"https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/05/28/world-bank-helps-bangladesh-provide-basic-services-opportunities-and-build-resilience-for-displaced-rohingya-and-host-co","summary":"The Bank approved projects for both Rohingya refugees and host communities, including health, nutrition, education, water, climate-resilient roads, renewable energy, disaster shelters, and women-focused safety measures. This is the strongest positive evidence that gains were being directed toward disadvantaged groups and neglected regions, though it was largely partner-led humanitarian development.","question_ids":["5B.8","5B.6"]},{"title":"Bangladesh - Inclusive Services and Opportunities for Host Communities and Displaced Rohingya Population Project","publisher":"World Bank","date":"May 3, 2024 / disclosed May 28, 2024","url":"https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099050924091537459","summary":"The project appraisal says the objective was to improve access to human capital services for vulnerable host communities and displaced Rohingya populations. This supports a limited fairness reading because it explicitly targets groups left behind, but it is not evidence of Hasina personally rebalancing national gains.","question_ids":["5B.8","5B.6"]},{"title":"UNFPA Bangladesh Annual Report","publisher":"UNFPA Bangladesh","date":"2024","url":"https://bangladesh.unfpa.org/en/unfpa-bangladesh-annual-report-2024","summary":"UNFPA reports targeted services for indigenous women, transgender people, sex workers, adolescent girls, and disaster-affected women, plus midwife support and GBV services. This is concrete inclusion evidence, but it is humanitarian service delivery rather than proof of a broad, fair distribution strategy by the ruler.","question_ids":["5B.8","5B.6","5B.7"]},{"title":"UNFPA and Japan sign $3.3 million assistance to Protect Rohingya Refugee and Host Community Women and girls in Cox's Bazar and Noakhali Districts","publisher":"UNFPA Bangladesh","date":"October 22, 2024","url":"https://bangladesh.unfpa.org/en/news/unfpa-and-japan-sign-33-million-assistance-protect-rohingya-refugee-and-host-community-women","summary":"This partnership targeted Rohingya refugee women/girls and host communities for protection, SRHR, and safe spaces. It shows some distribution toward highly vulnerable groups, but again it is external-partner driven and weakly attributable to Hasina.","question_ids":["5B.8","5B.6"]},{"title":"Rising Together: Empowering Women and Youth to Build Resilient Refugee and Host Communities in Bangladesh","publisher":"UNFPA Bangladesh","date":"December 1, 2024","url":"https://bangladesh.unfpa.org/en/news/rising-together-empowering-women-youth-build-resilient-refugee-and-host-communities","summary":"UNFPA and Switzerland framed the program as strengthening resilience and inclusion for Rohingya refugees and host communities, especially women and youth. This is another real but narrow positive for group-targeted support.","question_ids":["5B.8","5B.6"]},{"title":"35 million children in Bangladesh had schooling disrupted by Climate Crises in 2024","publisher":"UNICEF Bangladesh","date":"January 24, 2025","url":"https://www.unicef.org/bangladesh/en/press-releases/33-million-children-bangladesh-had-schooling-disrupted-climate-crises-2024unicef","summary":"UNICEF said climate shocks hit Bangladesh’s education system hard in 2024, with school closures and larger losses in poorer and climate-vulnerable districts. This is a useful contextual positive/partial item only in the sense that it shows the state had to confront geographically unequal shocks, not that it successfully equalized outcomes.","question_ids":["5B.8","5B.6"]},{"title":"Macro Poverty Outlook for Bangladesh: October 2024","publisher":"World Bank","date":"October 1, 2024","url":"https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099659510152422672","summary":"The World Bank projected extreme poverty up and inequality rising by more than one Gini point, with subdued investment and persistent social grievances. This is strong evidence against fair distribution of gains across classes and regions in 2024.","question_ids":["5B.8","5B.6","5B.3"]},{"title":"Bangladesh: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh/freedom-world/2024","summary":"Freedom House said minorities, refugees, and women remained underrepresented and faced discrimination, while Rohingya had limited access to health care, employment, and education and were subject to punitive camp policies. This is direct evidence against equitable distribution across groups.","question_ids":["5B.8","4B.7","5B.6"]},{"title":"Bangladesh country profile","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024/2025 profile page","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh","summary":"Freedom House says the Awami League consolidated power through harassment of opponents and co-optation of state institutions, with violence and discrimination against religious minorities and refugees remaining significant problems. This supports the inference that economic and social gains were not distributed neutrally.","question_ids":["5B.8","5B.5","4B.7"]},{"title":"World Bank Helps Bangladesh Provide Basic Services, Opportunities, and Build Resilience for Displaced Rohingya and Host Communities","publisher":"World Bank","date":"May 28, 2024","url":"https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/05/28/world-bank-helps-bangladesh-provide-basic-services-opportunities-and-build-resilience-for-displaced-rohingya-and-host-co","summary":"Even in a positive project, the Bank noted Rohingya live under severe pressure and host communities face limited resources, which underscores the need because gains were not naturally reaching those areas. This is weaker than the explicit positive read, but it still points to structural distributional imbalance.","question_ids":["5B.8"]},{"title":"World Report 2025: Bangladesh","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2025","url":"https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2025/country-chapters/bangladesh","summary":"HRW’s retrospective summary says 2024 ended with mass repression and attacks on Hindus, Ahmadiyya Muslims, and ethnic minorities after Hasina’s ouster. While this is partly post-Hasina, it reinforces that vulnerable groups were not protected by the distributional order in 2024.","question_ids":["5B.8","4B.7"]},{"title":"Vandalism, Attacks Follow Bangladesh Prime Minister’s Exit","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"August 8, 2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/08/vandalism-attacks-follow-bangladesh-prime-ministers-exit","summary":"HRW reported attacks on Hindus, Ahmadiyya Muslims, and ethnic minorities, with homes, temples, and businesses targeted after Hasina’s departure. That does not show fair or stable distribution across groups; if anything, it shows how fragile and uneven protection was in 2024.","question_ids":["5B.8","4B.7"]},{"title":"Bangladesh - Cash Transfer Modernization Project: Improving Transparency and Efficiency of Safety Nets","publisher":"World Bank","date":"January 1, 2024","url":"https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099739201032424234","summary":"The project profile notes cash transfers for the poorest and most socially excluded populations, including widows and older people. This is a limited positive signal for fairness, but it also implies Bangladesh still needed modernization to reach the poorest effectively.","question_ids":["5B.8","5B.6"]}]}
